topics.title: Supreme Court opens a packed new term
topics.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court began a new term with major cases expected on climate change, immigration, gun rights and religious rights.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a court term starts with huge issues lined up, who reads every preview and who waits for the actual decisions?

topics.title: Nobel medicine prize honors brain-light research
topics.summary: Three scientists won the Nobel Prize in medicine for work connected to optogenetics, a field that uses light to study and influence brain activity.
topics.discussionPrompt: If scientists can use light to understand the brain, who gets excited about the possibilities and who immediately asks about the limits?

topics.title: Markets hover near record highs
topics.summary: U.S. stocks rose near record levels, with technology shares helping lift the Nasdaq as investors waited for the next earnings season.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets are near records but everyone is waiting on earnings, who feels optimistic and who keeps checking the fine print?

topics.title: Southern California faces late heat
topics.summary: Extreme heat warnings covered parts of Southern California, with forecasts calling for temperatures in the high 30s Celsius during a late-season hot spell.
topics.discussionPrompt: When October suddenly acts like midsummer, who changes every plan and who insists they can still handle the patio?

topics.title: Black Sea grain ship attack raises concern
topics.summary: Ukraine said Russian drones hit a commercial vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea, adding fresh worry around shipping and food routes.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a food shipment becomes part of a war story, who thinks about global supply chains and who thinks about the crew first?

topics.title: Yemen forces retake areas near key strait
topics.summary: Officials said Saudi-backed Yemeni forces expelled Houthi rebels from several areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a major shipping corridor.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a faraway strait matters to world trade, who already knows the map and who needs someone to point at it dramatically?

topics.title: Museums try new licensing deals
topics.summary: Major museums are increasingly licensing collections and exhibitions for products, hotel suites and virtual reality as cultural institutions look for new revenue.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a museum collection shows up in VR or a hotel room, who calls it clever outreach and who worries it feels too commercial?

topics.title: Saturn reaches a prime viewing moment
topics.summary: Skywatchers are being encouraged to look for Saturn as it makes its closest approach to Earth this year, appearing as a creamy-white point.
topics.discussionPrompt: On a good Saturn night, who brings the telescope and who just wants someone else to say which dot is the planet?

topics.title: NASA highlights the Sombrero Galaxy
topics.summary: NASA's astronomy picture feature spotlighted the Sombrero Galaxy and its tidal streams, offering a striking look at how galaxies carry traces of past interactions.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a galaxy looks calm but carries evidence of old cosmic drama, who sees beauty and who starts asking what happened there?

topics.title: College football rankings keep shifting
topics.summary: AP college football coverage tracked another shakeup in the rankings, with early-season wins and upsets reshaping the national conversation.
topics.discussionPrompt: When rankings move around this much, who argues the whole list and who just wants their team to survive Saturday?
